text: Taking the first entry: write the plan for #1746. Checking the facts in the code first.
I took the first queued task, writing the plan for #1746 (an Actions agent is told two branch names). I've read the code; checking one more detail, then writing the plan.
Findings are in. Writing the plan to `agent-data`.
Two line numbers were off by a little; fixing them in the plan.

I wrote the plan for #1746, "An Actions agent is told two branch names". It's saved as `tickets/2026-08-28_actions-agent-two-branch-names.plan.md` on the `agent-data` branch. The task was a plan, not a code change, so there is no commit, pull request or merge.

I left the ticket open: closing it would have deleted the plan I just wrote, and the fix itself hasn't been done yet. I removed the queue entry and released my claim. My checkout is clean.

**What the plan found:**
- **No work is lost today.** The agent creates `agent-<name>` and commits there. The workflow then pushes those commits under the name the driver picked, `claude/actions-…`, and the `agent-<name>` branch disappears with the runner. Every turn picks up from the `claude/…` branch, so the work always ends up on that one branch. The real problems are the naming and an instruction the workflow undoes.
- **Two claims in the ticket are wrong on main:**
  - Cloud (web) sessions also end on their own `claude/*` branches, not on `agent-<name>`.
  - The cleanup in `@gemstack/skill-branches` (the "reclaim" step) only handles local checkouts. An Actions run keeps its work only on GitHub, so nothing is at risk. The only effect is that nothing lists or deletes the `claude/actions-*` branches.
- **Recommended fix:**
  - Set the branch prefix to `agent-` in `cli.ts:1136`, so the pushed branch follows the `agent-` naming.
  - Give Actions agents a short prompt that says "commit on the branch you are on", instead of `branch_yourself.md`.
  - The ticket says no code until the maintainer picks, since users see these branch names. The same question should ask whether Actions runs stay in the new scheduler design at all; if they don't, the cheapest answer is to just document it or close the ticket.
- **Scores:** effort 2, uncertainty 5.

Two tasks are still queued, both "write the plan": the dashboard architecture ticket and the Cursor parity checklist.

Separately, Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive need to be authorized in your claude.ai connector settings before I can use them.
